vo: July eighth changed where your cert data goes.
For most imports, certificate data is now eFiled at entry.
Not emailed later. Say a seller still keeps only a PDF in a folder.
The data comes from the certificate: product, rules, test lab and date, records contact.
Not sure which rules apply? Free CPSC finder. No account needed.
caption:
For most imports, July 8, 2026 moved certificate data from a folder to the customs entry.
Under 16 CFR 1110.13(a)(1), the certifier of an imported product eFiles the certificate data elements in ACE when the entry is filed. On imports, that's usually the importer.
Those elements come from the certificate itself: the product ID, each rule, the test lab and date, a records contact and more.
Mail imports go a different route: the data goes into CPSC's Product Registry before arrival.
Check the certificate before the entry, not after.

sources.claim: Imports: certificate data eFiled in ACE at entry
sources.quote: the finished product certifier must eFile the finished product certificate data elements required in § 1110.11 at the time of filing the entry, or the time of filing the entry and entry summary, if both are filed together, in ACE

sources.claim: Part 1110's eFiling text took effect July 8, 2026 (most imports; hedged 'most' because some entries, e.g. from Foreign Trade Zones, follow later)
On imports the importer is the certifier
sources.quote: Except as otherwise provided in a specific rule, ban, standard, or regulation enforced by CPSC, for a finished product manufactured outside of the United States that must be accompanied by a certificate as set forth in § 1110.5, the importer, as defined in this part, is the finished product certifier

sources.claim: Each certificate carries a product identifier
sources.quote: Finished product certificates must contain at least one of the following unique identifiers: global trade item number (GTIN), model number, registered number, serial number, stock keeping number (SKU), universal product code (UPC), or alternate identifier
Finished product certificates must identify separately all applicable rules, bans, standards, or regulations.

sources.claim: Certificate data: records contact, manufacture, test date and lab
sources.quote: (4) Identify and provide contact information ... for the individual maintaining records ... (5) Provide the date (month and year, at a minimum) and place ... where the finished product(s) were manufactured ... (6) Provide the most recent date and place(s) (including for each third party conformity assessment body ...) where the finished product(s) were tested

sources.claim: Mail imports: Product Registry before arrival
sources.quote: In the case of finished products that are manufactured outside of the United States and imported by mail, the finished product certifier must enter the finished product certificate data elements required in § 1110.11 into CPSC's Product Registry before arrival of the product or substance in the United States.
